issues.description: Method name/signature mismatch for course participation: the problem statement and the template expect an instance method attend(course:) on Developer, but the solution implements participateIn(course:) instead. Additionally, the solution's Client calls attend(course:) while the Developer implementation lacks that method, creating an internal inconsistency that will cause compilation errors and confuses students about which method to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make method names and signatures consistent across all artifacts. Rename the solution's participateIn(course:) method to attend(course:) (or update the template/problem and Client to use participateIn) so that Developer defines attend(course:) and Client calls attend(course:). Ensure the declaration in Developer.swift matches the template/problem statement exactly.

issues.description: The problem statement and template require a Developer method named attend(course:), but the solution implementation defines the method as participateIn(course:). This naming mismatch breaks the conceptual mapping (students expect to implement or call attend(course:)) and causes inconsistency between Client usage and Developer implementation in the solution repository.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the method participateIn(course:) in solution_repository/Sources/DeveloperLib/Developer.swift to attend(course:) so the method name matches the problem statement and the template. Alternatively, update Client to call participateIn, but the preferred fix is to standardize on attend(course:) across all artifacts.
